Has anyone encountered something like the following? The instance head clearly matches the first two #synth queries yet trace.Meta.synthInstance report the same

[Meta.synthInstance] ❌️ Decodable (Code.mk "list" 1 [Code.mk "nat" 0 [] ⋯] ⋯) BasicUniv ?m.9 ▼
  [] ✅️ no instances for Decodable (Code.mk "list" 1 [Code.mk "nat" 0 [] ⋯] ⋯) BasicUniv _tc.0 ▼
    [instances] #[]
  [] result <not-available>

error (modulo the type change). And when I choose any number n that doesn't satisfy the equation codes.length = n, the synthesis succeeds. Anyone have any clue what might be happening? Or some way to get more information out of the no instances trace. I'd write an #mwe but Code, Univ and DecodableGen depend on entire files!

class Decodable (code : Code) (univ : Univ) (type : outParam Type) : Prop where ...

class DecodableGen
  (typ : String) (tail revAcc : List Code)  (univ : Univ) (t : outParam (Type 1)) (type : outParam t) where

instance
  {univ : Univ}
  {f : String}
  {n : Nat}
  {codes : List Code}
  {α : Type}
  [DecodableGen f [] codes univ Type α]
  : Decodable (.mk f n codes (sorry : codes.length = n)) univ α := sorry

--these two immediately fail with error "No instances found for <type>"
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 1 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 2 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _

--all of these succeed
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 0 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 2 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 3 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _

#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 0 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 1 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 3 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _

A small excerpt from one of those successful syntheses shows that exactly the instance defined in this codeblock is immediately used to generate the new goals which make for a successful synthesis:

[Meta.synthInstance] ✅️ Decodable (Code.mk "list" 0 [Code.mk "nat" 0 [] ⋯] ⋯) BasicUniv (List ℕ) ▼
  [] ✅️ new goal Decodable (Code.mk "list" 0 [Code.mk "nat" 0 [] ⋯] ⋯) BasicUniv _tc.0 ▼
    [instances] #[@instDecodableMkOfDecodableGenNilCodeType]

Here is the full context. Like I said it is a bit big, but all of these are necessary to constitute the exact instance head of the instance causing a problem. Please let me know if there is anything I can explain, I've added some comments to explain some parts of the code.

import Std.Data.Internal.List.Defs
import Std.Data.Internal.List.Associative
import Mathlib.Data.W.Basic

open Std Internal

section DMapPrereqs -- DMap and Map fns used to define Univ. Used over hashmap types for easier decidability proofs and more straightforward reducibility

structure DMap (α : Type u) [BEq α] (β : α -> Type v) where
  toList : List ((a : α) × β a)
  distinctKeys : toList.DistinctKeys


def DMap.reverse
  [BEq α]
  [PartialEquivBEq α]
  (m : DMap α β)
  : DMap α β :=
  ⟨m.toList.reverse, sorry⟩

def DMap.Const.insertList
  [BEq α]
  [PartialEquivBEq α]
  (m : DMap α (fun (_ : α) => β)) (l : List (α × β)) : DMap α (fun (_ : α) => β) :=
  ⟨m.toList.insertListConst l, List.DistinctKeys.insertList m.distinctKeys⟩

instance [BEq α] : EmptyCollection (DMap α β) where
  emptyCollection := ⟨[], by simp⟩

def DMap.Const.ofList
  [BEq α]
  [PartialEquivBEq α]
  (l : List (α × β)) : DMap α (fun (_ : α) => β) :=
  (DMap.Const.insertList ∅ l).reverse

structure Map (α : Type u) [BEq α] (β : Type v) where
  inner : DMap α (fun (_ : α) => β)

def Map.ofList
  [BEq α]
  [PartialEquivBEq α]
  (l : List (α × β)) : Map α β :=
  ⟨DMap.Const.ofList l⟩

end DMapPrereqs

section TypeFnGen -- typeclass used to generate 'Type 1' types for making 'Univ' entries

class TypeFnGen (arity : Nat) (typ : outParam (Type 1)) where
  fn : (F : typ) -> Vector Type arity -> Type

instance : TypeFnGen 0 Type where
  fn := fun t _ => t

instance
  [inst : TypeFnGen n t]
  : TypeFnGen (Nat.succ n) (Type -> t) where
    fn := fun F v =>
      have := inst.fn
      this (F v.head) v.tail

def mkUnivEntry (typ : String) (arity : Nat) [TypeFnGen arity t] (F : t) : String ×  (n : Nat) × (Vector Type n -> Type) :=
  (typ, ⟨arity, TypeFnGen.fn F⟩)

end TypeFnGen


section Univ -- the 'Univ' datatype proper and the term (BasicUniv : Univ) involved in the typeclass synthesis issue

structure Univ where
  inner : Map String ((n : Nat) × (Vector Type n -> Type))

abbrev BasicUniv : Univ where
  inner := .ofList [
    (mkUnivEntry "nat" 0 Nat),
    (mkUnivEntry "bool" 0 Bool),
    (mkUnivEntry "unit" 0 Unit),
    (mkUnivEntry "empty" 0 Empty),
    (mkUnivEntry "string" 0 String),
    (mkUnivEntry "format" 0 Std.Format),
    (mkUnivEntry "arrow" 2 (· -> ·)),
    (mkUnivEntry "name" 0 Lean.Name),
    (mkUnivEntry "array" 1 Array),
    (mkUnivEntry "list" 1 List),
    (mkUnivEntry "prod" 2 Prod),
    (mkUnivEntry "option" 1 Option),
    ]

end Univ

section Code -- the 'Code' datatype used the encode types as data

def WType.Free (α : Type u) := WType fun x : α × Nat => Fin x.snd

abbrev Code := WType.Free String

abbrev Code.mk (typ : String) (arity : Nat) (subterms : List Code) (h : subterms.length = arity := by simp) : Code :=
  WType.mk (typ, arity) (h ▸ subterms.get)

end Code


section Decodable

-- given (code : Code) and (univ : Univ), provides a decoding (type : outParam Type) along with a proof that it is a valid decoding
class Decodable (code : Code) (univ : Univ) (type : outParam Type) : Prop where
  -- satisfies : univ.SatisfiedBy code -- proof that (code : Code) is decodable in (univ : Univ)
  -- wf : univ.decode code satisfies = type -- proof that (type : outParam Type) is the decoding of (code : Code)

-- used to generate a Decodable instance from a (⟨.ofList _⟩ : Univ) term
class DecodableGen
  (typ : String) (tail revAcc : List Code)  (univ : Univ) (t : outParam (Type 1)) (type : outParam t) where


-- preservation of decoding when 'List.cons'ing an entry
instance
  [DecodableGen typ tail [] ⟨.ofList es⟩ t α]
  : DecodableGen typ tail [] ⟨.ofList (e :: es)⟩ t α := sorry

-- preservation of decoding when the entry providing the decoding is the head, 'e'
instance
  [DecodableGen typ tail [] ⟨.ofList (e :: es)⟩ t α]
  : DecodableGen typ tail [] ⟨.ofList (e :: e' :: es)⟩ t α := sorry

-- this typeclass is used to generate a proof that a type function of type (Type -> Type : Type 1) or more generally (Type -> ... : Type 1) is part of the universe
class IsUnivType (typ : String) (univ : Univ) (t : outParam (Type 1)) (type : outParam t) where

-- base case
instance [TypeFnGen arity t] : IsUnivType type ⟨.ofList [mkUnivEntry type arity T]⟩ t T := sorry

-- preservation when extending the univ
instance
  [IsUnivType typ ⟨.ofList es⟩ t T]
  : IsUnivType typ ⟨.ofList (e :: es)⟩ t T := sorry

-- preservation when decoding is provided by the head, 'e'
instance
  [IsUnivType typ ⟨.ofList (e :: es)⟩ t T]
  : IsUnivType typ ⟨.ofList (e :: e' :: es)⟩ t T := sorry

instance
  [IsUnivType f univ t F]
  : DecodableGen f [] [] univ t F := sorry

/- examples
#synth IsUnivType "list" BasicUniv (Type -> Type) List
#synth DecodableGen "list" [] [] BasicUniv (Type -> Type) List
-/

instance
  {t : Type 1}
  {F : Type -> t}
  [DecodableGen f codes [] univ (Type -> t) F]
  [DecodableGen typ [] [] univ Type α]
  : DecodableGen f (.mk typ 0 [] :: codes) [] univ t (F α) := sorry

-- reverses the list of codes (which are used to make the final code's tail) so that the type matches the code
instance
  [DecodableGen f (code :: codes) acc univ Type α]
  : DecodableGen f codes (code :: acc) univ Type α := sorry

/-
some more examples
#synth DecodableGen "bool" [] [] BasicUniv Type Bool
#synth DecodableGen "list" [.mk "bool" 0 []] [] BasicUniv _ (List Bool)
#synth DecodableGen "prod" [.mk "nat" 0 [], .mk "bool" 0 []] [] BasicUniv _ _
#synth DecodableGen "prod" [.mk "nat" 0 [], .mk "bool" 0 []] [] BasicUniv Type (Prod Bool Nat)
#synth DecodableGen "prod" [.mk "bool" 0 []] [.mk "nat" 0 []] BasicUniv Type (Prod Bool Nat)
-/


--the instance having an issue:
instance
  {univ : Univ}
  {f : String}
  {n : Nat}
  {codes : List Code}
  {α : Type}
  [DecodableGen f [] codes univ Type α]
  : Decodable (.mk f n codes (sorry : codes.length = n)) univ α := sorry


--these two immediately fail with error "No instances found for <type>"
set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 1 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 2 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _

--all of these succeed
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 0 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 2 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "list" 3 [.mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _

#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 0 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 1 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _
#synth Decodable (.mk "prod" 3 [.mk "bool" 0 [], .mk "nat" 0 []] sorry) BasicUniv _

The exact issue seems to be caused by the behaviour of Lean.Meta.DiscrTree.getUnify:

open Lean Elab Term Command
open Meta
open Qq

elab "debugterm1" : term => do
  let insts <- getGlobalInstancesIndex
  let hExpr' <- mkFreshExprMVarQ q(List.length (α := Code) [] = 0)
  let hExpr <- mkFreshExprMVarQ q(List.length [Code.mk "nat" 0 [] $hExpr'] = 1)
  let αExpr <- mkFreshExprMVarQ q(Type)
  let expr := q(Decodable (Code.mk "list" 1 [Code.mk "nat" 0 [] $hExpr'] $hExpr) BasicUniv $αExpr)
  let r <- insts.getUnify expr
  if r.size = 0 then dbg_trace "no entry unifies"
  for i in r do dbg_trace i.globalName?
  return q(Nat)

def x : debugterm1 := 5 -- no entry unifies

elab "debugterm2" : term => do
  let insts <- getGlobalInstancesIndex
  let αExpr <- mkFreshExprMVarQ q(Type)
  let codesExpr <- mkFreshExprMVarQ q(List Code)
  let hExpr <- mkFreshExprMVarQ q(List.length $codesExpr = 1)
  let expr := q(Decodable (Code.mk "list" 1 $codesExpr $hExpr) BasicUniv $αExpr)
  let r <- insts.getUnify expr
  if r.size = 0 then dbg_trace "no entry unifies"
  for i in r do dbg_trace i.globalName?
  return q(Nat)

def x' : debugterm2 := 5 -- (some myinst)

can someone confirm whether this is expected behaviour?

To help debugging, you can use #discr_tree_key to see the discrimination tree keys of an instance:

/-
Decodable
  (@WType.mk (Prod String ℕ) _ (@Prod.mk String ℕ _ _) (@Eq.rec ℕ _ _ (@List.get (WType.Free String) _) _ _))
  _
  _
-/
#discr_tree_key instDecodableMkOfDecodableGenNilCodeType

This contains the somewhat suspicious looking Eq.rec that appears in the definition of Code.mk.

Ah fantastic good catch! that turned out to be the issue. A slightly modified version of Code.mk made synthesis work normally:

abbrev Code.mk (typ : String) (arity : Nat) (subterms : List Code) (h : subterms.length = arity := by simp) : Code :=
  WType.mk (typ, arity) fun x => subterms.get (h ▸ x)

(moved the equality cast inside the WType's tail)
Small note, you probably will want to use Fin.cast instead of the Eq.rec
